messages.author: f0ce474d9924d57a
messages.subject: timing each iteration in stan?
parts:
Hi!

We are trying to understand why one model runs much more quickly than a similar model. Is there a way to get Stan to return the time taken on each iteration, or the time taken to perform each gradient evaluation? 

Thanks very much,
Emma Pierson

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] timing each iteration in stan?
parts:
Those aren't the same. The run time is going to be
a factor of multiple things:

iteration / n_eff --- how well it mixes

leapfrog / iteration --- how many leapfrog steps per iteration

seconds / leapfrog --- how long the log density and gradients take

And warmup works completely differently from sampling (it's more herky-jerky
as it finds its way to an adapted state).

You can get number of leapfrog steps per iteration out of the interfaces
and do your own timing and we report n_eff.

There's variation across chains with the same model depending on
random seed for initialization and initial moves.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] timing each iteration in stan?
parts:
The time per gradient evaluation is constant across
the history of a chain and is almost always large enough
to dominate any overhead, so you can get a pretty good
estimate of the time per gradient evaluation by dividing
the sampling time by the sum of n_leapfrog_ over all
sampling iterations.
